q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT f1.drinker AS drinkerA, f2.drinker AS drinkerB FROM frequents AS f1 JOIN frequents AS f2 ON f1.bar = f2.bar AND f1.drinker < f2.drinker GROUP BY f1.drinker, f2.drinker HAVING COUNT(f1.bar) = COUNT(f2.bar)

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 compares the total times a week each drinker frequents any bar, while Q2 compares the number of bars each drinker frequents with the same number of bars another drinker frequents.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have two drinkers, A and B, who frequent the same number of bars, but A frequents the same bar more times a week than B.
